_comment: Shared fixture for the convergence computations that exist twice.
profileOf / cosine (TypeScript) are the same functions written twice, and
`_converging`'s docstring asserts they mirror each other exactly. They did
not: the TS side filtered profile entries to `w > 0`, so two parties who
both OPPOSE the same thing had their profiles emptied and disappeared from
the pane while scoring +1 in the query bar, and any mixed profile lost its
A docstring claiming two implementations agree is how they came to
disagree. This file is the claim, in numbers, and both suites assert
against it. Add a case here before changing either implementation.
`distance_penalties` used to live here. The penalty is GONE from both
sides: it multiplied affinity by distance, which capped `converge>` at
0.5 forever because sharing an interest puts two actors at exactly two
hops. It was a set difference written as a multiplication. Affinity and
contact are now two separate tests over the same pair — `converge` and
`contact` — so there is no combined number left to keep in parity.

profiles.name: a plain positive profile passes through
negatives are KEPT — opposition is half the signal
an entry that cancelled to zero is dropped, not kept as weak
a profile that is all zeros is no profile at all
an empty map is no profile

cosines.name: both SERVE the same interest — allies
both OPPOSE the same interest — they do agree
one serves, one opposes — adversaries, and the sign says so
a mixed profile keeps BOTH halves in the dot product
dropping the negative half would have scored this 1.0
an empty profile yields zero rather than a division
